spans.text: What is this place...?
Anna...
Who's calling me?
It's me, Uncle Powell.
You're heading out today. Don't you remember?
Heading out?
Yes, heading out to your new home.
See, your mother and father from your new family have come to pick you up.
Come, be good and take your medicine, then you can leave this place and go to your new home.
I don't want to leave this place! I want to be with everyone!
Don't cry, Anna. Everyone will be going with you.
Anna looks back and sees countless wooden crates behind her, all sized to fit a child.
While she knows that the children lying in these crates are just sleeping, she can't shake the thought that the crates are their coffins.
No! I don't want to!
Pills are stuffed into Anna's mouth, and the tip of her tongue is numbed by the bitterness.
Shhh... Remember the story I told you?
Each child is a seed of infinite potential.
Some seeds blossom into beautiful flowers right after being planted. Others need to go through a long period of growing before they can bloom.
But what I forgot to tell you is that some seeds are destined to grow in the darkness forever...
For ever and ever, until they rot in the dirt...
No, no...
Z-W Pharma's third-floor office area.
Anna, Anna!
You're finally awake.
Are you alright? Do you feel uncomfortable anywhere?
I'm fine...
We're both sleeping, but why is it that when Anna wakes up, everyone falls over themselves to see if she's okay, but when I do, I get beaten up instead...
Anna's still a child, after all, and you're an experienced wageslave.
Also, I haven't docked your pay for sleeping on the job yet.
Ugh...
45, I remembered something important...
At the Griffin temporary base.
...In other words, most of the Nyto test subjects in the underground labs within the Paldiski Submarine Base came from orphanages.
William was working with them; the orphanages would routinely send their children to William for use in experiments.
And this Powell is an intermediary between William and the orphanages.
Correct. We'll just have to wait for Ange to follow up on the lead.
It was truly a masterful move.
Nobody would care about the kids abandoned in the orphanages, who would be completely defenseless, ripe for the picking.
Moreover, orphanages everywhere have always suffered from overcrowding, so nobody would notice a few missing kids...
To put it more ruthlessly, it would be a surefire moneymaker.
And I suppose this drug plant also played a supporting role in all of this?
In order to improve the survival rate of the children he was transporting, William directed Zeratul-Worcester Pharmaceuticals to produce a forbidden drug.
This drug would slow the children's breathing and keep them asleep in their crates.
It wouldn't beat a proper inspection, but it would be more than enough to help them slip past minor checkpoints.
In my experience, it's pretty easy to buy off the inspectors at those checkpoints.
If they knew what was in those crates...would they be able to sleep at night?
Commander, not all humans have hearts.
I believe you would know that better than myself.
I've sent the drugs you brought back to the labs for chemical analysis.

According to Anna's testimony, those drugs have obvious flaws. Some of the kids would wake up mid-transit and start scrabbling and hyperventilating wildly when they find themselves locked inside a crate, which only has a limited supply of oxygen...
While others would take the drugs and never wake up...
There's no telling if the children who died early in the crates were luckier than those who survived the ravaging experiments...
I'm sorry for sending you to such a place of bloody evil.
The place was cleaned up very well.
But for the people involved, no amount of cleaning would get rid of the blood, filth and sin on their hands.
That's it for my report.
Now I shall get back to the Griffin reconstruction mission.
Alright. Thank you.
UMP45 leaves the office.
The Commander turns to look at Anna, who's playing outside the window.
There's no hint of gloominess on her innocent, childish smile.
That's the kind of smile a child should have.
